preamble: Replacement of a rhotic by the labio-velar glide [w]. Its best-documented occurrence is 'gliding of liquids' in English-speaking children's phonological development (rabbit > [wæbɪt]); as an adult or historical sound change it is not established (the adult southern British variant is labiodental [ʋ], not [w]).

examples.note: Gliding of liquids, a typical phonological process in early acquisition.
